chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: The management contract with Gladys Mosier and Claude Thornhill
summary: They drew up a contract as personal representatives with 25 percent each; little came of it at first, and Kirby managed himself.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: And your good luck and the good luck of the Onyx Club in hiring you to perform there. And that's around the time you went into this partnership with Gladys Mosier and Thornhill.
When I met Gladys and Claude that day, we had a contract already drawn up which I signed, in fact Jenny and I both signed the contract,
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
that they were supposed to be our personal representatives. I think the commission or something, whatever they wanted would amount to about twenty-five percent of our earnings.

Yeah, which in the first few months didn't amount to anything because we weren't making that much money. But Claude was definitely interested and he went to work right away to see what he could do to promote. At that particular time I had no business sense or what he may have been able to see in my performances, but he did do everything that he could. The first thing he did was arrange for the recording that I made with his band on which we did 'Gone With The Wind'. And then he arranged for me to do a lot of transcriptions for the BBC. And of course there were a lot of musicians that hung out at the Ongx Club at that time so they may have seen the possibility, you know, that I didn't realize, had any real financial value. I was just having a good time and glad to be having the work. Of course you know that he arranged, made the arrangement with "Loch Lomond" and during that time John Kirby had just time to get his group together. And I had
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

been singing in the intermission and Jenny at the piano, and myself. So he arranged for me to make recordings with the group. And then, after that I became the singer with the group because Claude proceeded to make arrangements for me.
Did he manage the Kirby Band also, in any way?

No, not really, Kirby did his own managing. I would think that maybe Joe Helback, the owner of the Club, decided that it would be better for me to sing with the orchestra. And things just happened, you know, one right after the other. As I said before, I had exposure on the broadcasting system. They were swinging at its peak then. I had appeared on the program called the Saturday Night Swing Club. And all this time I was getting all this exposure. And then, of course, when I did 'Loch Lomond' on the air and it was cut off with the station manager in Detroit, then it really became controversial and sort of a national type phenomenon. And that's when everybody got busy, you know, deciding exactly what they were going to do about me.
